fAssessment.sourceReview: Component is display-only; actions invoke only the four navigation names. No network/model/native/command starts in TrialWorkspace. Unknown/fixture/readonly and configuration-only wording remain distinct; raw readiness counts do not become execution grants. Project rows do not become selectors or new authority. React text rendering and trialProbeError mapping avoid raw error stack/credential output in the standard hook path. CSS stays in trial-* subtree and uses existing tokens.
fAssessment.hookScope: Reload/unmount/disable effect cleanup ignores prior requests and prior valid observation is kept during refresh/error. Transport is normally one stable main instance. The hook depends on capability presence rather than transport identity; replacing an enabled transport instance with another instance having readiness requires explicit reload/remount. This replacement scenario was not executed in this review and is a consumer precondition/residual coverage boundary, not a claimed current-main bypass.
fAssessment.independentBrowserScope: No candidate browser suite was rerun. Candidate22 state/6HTTP/6app-target records and screenshots retain their submitted measured scope; they do not substitute for main's actual App composition/browser acceptance.
fAssessment.requiredMainComposition: Main owns App/transport/route/four navigation target mapping and must validate the actual mounted experience, keyboard/desktop/mobile and zero-send behavior. Do not import F test harness or controlled fixtures into runtime.

gAssessment.preservedGoodScope: Schema reuse, deterministic summary, outcome-id replay/conflict handling, exact outcome project/window exclusion, per-layer/per-currency rows, partial UI-review proxy, explicit known/unknown values, operator baseline separation, loopback-only explicit credential/redirect refusal, request timeout and exclusive0600 output all have useful source/tests. No new price/model/SQL/runtime authority is present.
gAssessment.integrationRecommendation: F can be integrated independently with insights omitted/unavailable. G types/source may be staged in a nondispatching optional package, but unrestricted real-data complete summaries/intervention/attention reports should remain outside the default UI until scope/coverage/bounds findings close. A narrowly composed main consumer must independently scope and validate every admitted source and preserve unavailable intervention/attention states; do not merely rely on G's current complete badge.

findings.problem: Only outcomes and queue facts are project/window filtered. Every parsed WorkEvidence entry is passed to workInterventions regardless of event.at or proven project mapping, and all attention items enter attentionSummary without declared-project filtering. CLI project/window overrides therefore do not scope all metrics. Four independent valid-data negatives demonstrate foreign project, old event, unmapped work and foreign attention contamination.
findings.requiredOutcome: Create one validated project/work/contract source map and enforce declared scope on all record classes; unmapped work cannot become an observed in-scope zero/count. Apply the requested event-time window to historical intervention facts; attention remains a separately declared current snapshot but must obey project scope and explicit observation freshness. Preserve exact outcome/layer/currency handling and original provenance.

findings.problem: workParsed invalid/quarantined signal downgrades outcomes but not workCoverage. After every work record is invalid, interventionMetrics sees an empty complete set and emits a measured0 with unknown0 and complete coverage. This contradicts the module's null/unknown promise and can produce false efficiency conclusions even though global quarantine is nonzero.
findings.requiredOutcome: Propagate invalid/conflicted/missing sources into the appropriate per-source and per-metric coverage/unknown counts. Keep genuine complete empty windows as zero only when emptiness is positively established, not when records were rejected. Test all-invalid and mixed valid/invalid work and attention sources.

findings.problem: Unknown-length successful bodies are fully arrayBuffer'ed before byte accounting/refusal; error bodies are also fully drained without a byte bound. A maxBytes1024 client buffers all131072 bytes in a finite private response before failing. Content-Length checks cover only cooperative declared lengths, not the resource bound advertised by the collector.
findings.requiredOutcome: Read/cancel body streams under a remaining-byte budget before full allocation; apply bounded handling to non2xx and redirect bodies too. Keep per-request/overall deadlines, explicit origin/token/redirect constraints, and test absent/false Content-Length with an original small positive.

findings.problem: appliedLimits reports stoppedBy based on counts after analysis but does not enforce declared limits or downgrade coverage. maxRecords1 still accepts2 and reports complete. Configured maxWorks/maxPages/bytes similarly need an enforceable meaning or explicit declaration that they are collector observations, not applied bounds.
findings.requiredOutcome: Validate/enforce supported limits before expensive parsing/aggregation or reject inputs exceeding them. Partial processing must deterministically mark affected coverage and counts; exact-bound completion must not be mislabeled stopped. Keep schema-level hard caps as a separate guarantee.
